tickets.title: Cross-tab refresh-token mutex (single-use rotation double-spend)
tickets.summary: Found 2026-07-13 via api access log during the T-154.1 pause: two editor tabs share the single-use refresh token; tab A rotates it, tab B later POSTs the stale one -> /auth/refresh 401 -> the whole browser session dies (log: 12:13 local, registry+compat 401 -> refresh 401 -> all subsequent 401). The single-flight helper (apps/website/frontend/src/api/refresh.ts) serializes refreshes WITHIN a tab only. Fix: cross-tab mutex around refresh (Web Locks API, BroadcastChannel fallback) + adopt the rotated pair from the winning tab (storage event), so N tabs spend one rotation. Repro: open the editor in two tabs, wait out the access TTL, act in the stale tab.

tickets.summary: Rebuild the Arma 3 mission workflow inside Reforger: website Mission Creator = Eden, compiled mission JSON = the .pbo, and the mod supplies everything Reforger does NOT ship (lobby, briefing, slotting, spawn, spectator, admin). Stage 1 FACTORY shipped: host-aware execution, a 1.3s headless Enfusion compile gate on the native dedicated server (no Workbench), a mechanical CRF symbol index (266 files / 71,606 LOC), and a capability matrix whose UNTRIAGED gate turns a forgotten capability into a build error. Stage 2 is the TBD-owned event spine (ONE LIFE + admin respawn; macOS-methodology UI on Aegis tokens). CRF is an Arma-Public-License ORACLE — indexed, never vendored. ABSORBS T-068.13. BLOCKED: the only remaining slice is T-181.16 (executor: human) — a live two-client E2E on a dedicated server. Not agent-actionable; moved off `ready` on 2026-07-26 so the fleet does not pick it up.

T-181.3.notes: enf carve + index vanilla + make enf-carve. PARTIAL BY NATURE: only a subset of vanilla script ships uncompressed. T-181.3.2.notes: enf extract — pulls vanilla scripts BY REAL PATH from the pak FILE table (operator asked 'what about the MCP?' — the MCP's game_browse DOES list them; its game_read fails). T-181.9.notes: Slotting authority completed. ClaimSlot already existed (PS-shaped first-come guard). Added: ReleaseSlot (lobby-only change-of-mind; refused once deployed), BuildSlotRoster (per-slot key/faction/group/role/state/holder as TSV — the data T-181.9.1's picker binds to, deliberately plain text so authority is testable from the server log before any widget exists; state = OPEN|HELD|DEAD), and a ONE-LIFE INTEGRITY FIX: ClaimSlot and ReleaseSlot now both refuse a dead player. Without it a dead player could release their slot and claim a fresh one, bypassing one life entirely. Landmine caught by the compile gate in 1.3s: `out` is a RESERVED KEYWORD in Enfusion (out-param modifier) and cannot be a variable name.

T-181.9.1.notes: Lobby slot picker @ 56ad6d16. SUPERSEDES T-068.13. Server-fed roster parsed from BuildSlotRoster() and nothing else, so it cannot disagree with the authority. Optimistic claim held as a pending intent keyed on the slot until the authority rules on THAT seat — without it a refresh in flight makes the seat flicker away and back, which reads exactly like losing it. Refusal names the actual winner off the authority's own roster. Deploy is deliberately NOT optimistic. Back button hidden (the stack is empty beneath LOBBY, so 'back' is a trap). Deliberately does NOT filter the other side — you cannot pick a side you cannot see; side discipline starts at the briefing. m_bAutoDeploy REPORTED not flipped: the wave is currently the only working way into the world.

T-181.9.2.notes: Briefing screen @ d42eb681. Side discipline enforced AT THE WIRE: clients hold no mission document at all, the enemy ORBAT is never serialised, delivery is RplRcver.Owner, and the request carries no faction so a modified client cannot ask for the other side. ORBAT derived from slots[] not orbat{} because the latter models only roles/count, dropping callsign/slot/kit. GAP: `briefings` prose is unparsed — the screen shows structure without orders (T-181.23).

T-181.10.notes: JSON loadouts @ 4b1ff732. optic+magazine were parsed and DISCARDED — now mounted into weapon storage. Honest per-field failure lines naming slot+item; nakedness guard. Closed a real hole: body reuse now keyed on IDENTITY, so a player taking a vacated slot cannot inherit the previous occupant's fired mags/damage, while a mid-life reconnect still gets its own body. AdminRespawn forces a fresh body. IsBodyDead treated a missing CharacterControllerComponent as ALIVE (bug). COMPILE-VERIFIED ONLY — magazine chambering and optic mounting need eyes.

T-181.11.notes: ONE LIFE in TBD_SpawnManager: m_bOneLife attribute (default on), m_mDeadPlayers map, OnPlayerKilled now terminal — slot STAYS claimed so the seat is not recycled and reconnect still resolves. Added IsPlayerDead() and CountAliveForFaction() (the primitive T-181.13 side-eliminated needs; counts claimed slots so a never-deployed player cannot silently end the round). m_bAutoDeploy path retained for PIE.

T-181.11.1.notes: AdminRespawn(playerId, byAdmin) — server-authority only, refuses non-dead and disconnected players, re-materializes a dressed body on the player's own slot, writes an audit line, and re-marks dead on FAILED rather than leaving limbo. Chat: `#tbd respawn <playerId>` and `#tbd dead`. Permission reuses vanilla SCR_PlayerListedAdminManagerComponent.IsPlayerOnAdminList (so T-181.11.1 permissions were already HAVE).

T-181.11.2.notes: Admin menu @ c4708f72. A FRONT-END onto the same server authority as the chat commands, not a second implementation — TBD_AdminService is the single choke point and permission is checked at four entry points including the READ gate, so a non-admin's snapshot contains a refusal string and nothing else (no roster to render even with a patched client). Deploy and Respawn deliberately kept separate: AdminRespawn refuses anyone not dead and DeployPlayerEx refuses anyone who is, so one button would silently no-op half the time. Force-stage is armed-then-confirmed. Audit ring is capped at 60 with repeat refusals console-only, so a client spamming refusals cannot flush real actions out of an admin's view. Avoided a 4th modded SCR_PlayerController by extending the existing block. PERMISSION IS PROVEN BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY A LIVE NON-ADMIN ATTEMPT — needs the operator.

T-181.12.notes: Spectator @ 3845765e. Camera REIMPLEMENTED not derived, justified: SCR_ManualCamera's behaviour lives in a prefab (same rdb blocker for nothing), it is the editor camera, and it cannot follow. Reuses vanilla's ManualCameraContext actions so FREE FLIGHT WORKS BEFORE ANY WORKBENCH PASS. Faction-restricted by default: under one life half the server ends up spectating while still in squad voice, so unrestricted is a live intel feed, not a viewer. Client-side poll for enter/exit because 'am I spectating' is a client question — also covers reconnect-on-spent-life, which no death hook sees. HOOK NEEDED: spectator host entity for streaming (see T-181.24).

T-181.13.notes: JSON-driven round end. TBD_MissionWinConditionsStruct {mode, endOn[]} added to the mission document (@contract mission.schema.json#/$defs/winConditions) + TBD_MissionLoader.HasEndTrigger(). TickWinConditions in TBD_FrameworkManager (2s, armed only on LIVE and only if the mission declared faction_eliminated). Guards: ignores factions with 0 claimed slots (unfielded != eliminated), requires >=2 contesting factions (a solo test cannot end the round), unregisters itself off LIVE. time_limit and the other three enum triggers parse but are not evaluated yet — declared, not silently dropped.

T-181.13.1.notes: Results POST + the validator MAJOR. Validator warnings across the four goldens 28 -> 3 (bridgehead 18->0, empty-warning-fields 7->2, slot-loadout-coverage 2->0, montfort 1->1 unrelated); baseline tightened. CORRECTED A LANDMINE THE COMMAND CENTER WROTE: an instrumented boot dumping per-slot null/count state showed `ref array<>` is NOT over-allocated when the key is absent — cargo came back non-null on exactly the slots authoring a cargo key and null on those that did not, BOTH POLARITIES IN ONE RUN — while `ref <class>` is allocated regardless. The doc had said the distinction did not matter and not to spend a run on it; it matters, and the agent got it free from a run it had to do anyway. That fact is load-bearing: gear presence is genuinely unobservable (absent gear and gear:{} both parse to ten empty strings) but cargo presence is PROOF the block was authored, which is what finally makes the 'neither gear nor cargo' branch reachable. Results: no new endpoint, no Rust change; omits unmeasured stats rather than sending zeros, because absent says 'not measured' where 0 claims 'measured, and none'. outcome=success only when faction_eliminated was declared AND the arithmetic resolved. LIVE END-TO-END POST PROVED against a capture endpoint mirroring telemetry.rs: two real requests from 'Arma Reforger/1.7.0.54 (Headless; LINUX)', all 9 and 15 contract checks passed, hostile role label escaped correctly. Measured: the engine sends the body Transfer-Encoding: CHUNKED, so a receiver reading Content-Length sees an empty body. Shared accessor for T-181.35 is TBD_PlayerIdentity.GetArmaId — it deliberately returns EMPTY rather than a player:<id> lease, and such players are dropped, because users.arma_id is UNIQUE and empty ids would collapse rows and bind one account to everybody. ATTENDANCE INERT until T-181.35; LogIdentityCensus prints the no-op every round.

T-181.14.notes: Mission validation @ 915b78a8. TBD_MissionValidator (27 checks, all run in one pass, ERROR vs WARNING) + TBD_Log. Rejected mission holds the server in LOADING via the existing IsValid gate — no FrameworkManager edit. '#tbd validate' replays findings in game; every #tbd reply leads with a failure banner. Decision table verified offline against both golden missions + 14 mutations (proves the table, NOT the Enfusion runtime). Needs a hook: TBD_Log.Stage(prev,next) has no caller.

T-181.15.notes: JIP / reconnect hardened. Requirement 1 was ALREADY implemented — this made it survivable. THE REAL HAZARD WAS THE CALLQUEUE, which no prior audit had touched: five deferred callbacks carried a raw playerId across disconnect, and ScriptCallQueue.Remove cancels by FUNCTION so one player's timer cannot be cancelled alone. Worst case measured: RedeployAfterDeath would DEPLOY a fresh joiner into a dead player's slot. Closed with a lazily-opened connection epoch (lazy because vanilla only self-audits Listen && playerId>1, so a listen host's player 1 may never hit the join hook and stamping 0 would make its retry ladder permanently inert). Every int-keyed per-player map was audited and found SAFE — all erased on disconnect. The player:<id> residual was WORSE than recorded: it leaked the seat AND the life, so a recycled id arrived DEAD. Closed by splitting IsIdentityKey (backend or synthesized) from IsDurableKey (backend only) — having only one predicate is what caused it. JIP DECISION: deploy at any stage LOBBY..LIVE, because a player who crashed before deploying is INDISTINGUISHABLE at the join hook from a walk-up latecomer, so a 'too late' rule cannot be written that does not also strand the crash. One-life guard still protects the invariant. OPERATOR CAVEAT: in keyMode=NUMERIC a reconnector gets a SECOND seat, so CountClaimedForFaction over-counts — another reason a dedicated server with real identities is required for an event. COMPILE-VERIFIED ONLY: every behavioural claim needs a dedicated server + 2 clients; PIE cannot exercise any of it. Also unanswerable from this lane: whether SCR_ReconnectComponent is on GameMode_Plain.et (a prefab question) — the code is correct either way.

T-181.16.notes: Dedicated server + 2 real clients, full loop.

T-181.17.notes: Safestart / warmup phase. Damage suppressed via EnableDamageHandling(false) with VERIFIED restoration and a watchdog, so a failed restore cannot leave an event permanently invulnerable. Admin surface: '#tbd safestart [status|go|<seconds>]' answers 'is damage actually off right now' in one command. THE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS SLICE PRODUCED WAS A HOLE, NOT A FEATURE: the agent reported that it could not verify its component instantiates, because -scenarioId alone does not load the world on the headless server. Chasing that found the real cause — -config and -addons are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, and -addons+-scenarioId with no -config prints 'Game successfully created' and then idles without ever hosting. Three slices had by then added components to TBD_GameMode.et with NOTHING proving any of them instantiates. Closed by T-181.17.1.

T-181.17.1.notes: World-boot gate. Closes the hole T-181.17 surfaced: nothing proved the components on TBD_GameMode.et instantiate, and the compile gate is blind to prefab wiring. Two engine landmines found and recorded — -config and -addons are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (hard fatal), and -addons+-scenarioId with no -config prints 'Game successfully created' then idles without ever hosting, which is why the earlier harness 'proved' nothing. Working recipe: -addonsDir + -config with the addon in game.mods[] keyed by the addon.gproj GUID. Added TBD_FrameworkManager.PrintComponentRollCall() + scripts/mod/world-boot.sh, wired into wave.sh gate. ALL FIVE COMPONENTS VERIFIED PRESENT. HARDENED AFTER THE WAVE-4 VERIFIER BROKE IT: the roll-call alone passed a prefab containing TBD_ThisComponentDoesNotExist (it only checks names it was told about), so the gate now also greps the engine's own name-independent 'WORLD (E): Unknown class'; error attribution was classifying by MESSAGE TEXT and let six genuine TBD failures through (one differing only in the case of Scripts/Game/), so triage is now fail-closed with an explicit vanilla allowlist; Print(localVar) emits the DECLARATION not the value, so the selftest fixtures had never matched reality; added OnDelete to cancel four callqueue entries that survived an in-process scenario restart; ports randomised off the dev config so the gate no longer collides with the operator's server or a parallel run (proven with two concurrent boots). Selftest now pins 10 cases. NOT runtime evidence: the boot has no backend, so the stage machine never leaves LOADING.

T-181.18.notes: AO / play-area poly-zones + out-of-bounds. Polygon parsing added (ref array<ref array<float>>) — polygon zones previously parsed to nothing. TBD_ZoneGeometry (circle + crossing-number polygon), TBD_Zone, TBD_ZoneRegistry, TBD_PlayAreaComponent (1 Hz server tick, warn -> grace -> penalty). Terminal penalty implemented in full but OFF by default (rules.penalty defaults to 'warn'); a kill routes through SCR_CharacterDamageManagerComponent.Kill so it lands in the existing OnPlayerKilled -> MarkLifeSpent path — no second death path, TBD_SpawnManager untouched. OPERATOR-VISIBLE: golden-missions/bridgehead-at-levie.json zone z4 already authors penalty=kill graceSeconds=30, so the REFERENCE MISSION will permanently remove a player 30 s after they leave the AO. Geometry proven with 25 runtime cases via a shadow addon incl. concave notch, both winding orders, rays through vertices — with a deliberately-wrong expectation confirming the harness can print FAIL. FOUND A MAJOR LANDMINE: JsonLoadContext allocates nested ref struct fields even when the JSON key is ABSENT, so a null check is not a presence test. Also fixed a latent dead guard in GetSpawnZoneForFaction that would have returned map-corner (0,0) for a polygon spawn zone. NOT runtime-verified: no player ever joins under world-boot, so no enforcement path has run against a real player.

T-181.19.notes: Map markers from mission JSON. Consumer only — T-181.23 already parsed them and nothing read them. Rides Reforger's own SCR_MapMarkerManagerComponent.InsertStaticMarker with PLACED_CUSTOM, matching vanilla SCR_BaseTutorialStage.CreateMarkerCustom and CRF's own usage, so NO new .conf/.layout and the rdb blocker does not apply. PER-FACTION ENFORCEMENT IS STRUCTURAL: the request RPC takes NO ARGUMENTS, so a client cannot phrase the question; the side is read server-side from the assigned slot; reply is RplRcver.Owner; client insert is isLocal so received markers cannot re-enter replication. No slot = served=false, zero rows (fail closed). Discovered the icon enum vocabulary BY COMPILATION (23 members) rather than guessing, and resolves against the engine's own 91 placed icons first so all 91 are authorable with no maintenance. Corrected the command center's brief: 'all four fields required so a marker is complete' is true of PRESENCE, false of CONTENT — icon/label have no minLength and empty-warning-fields.json ships a marker with both empty. NOT runtime-observed: nothing visual, no client ever joined. Adds a 5th modded class SCR_PlayerController (overrides no vanilla method, adds no menu preset enum). || POST-MERGE (wave-5 verifier, MINOR, not yet fixed): a slot CHANGE leaves the previous side's markers on the client's map. TBD_SpawnManager.ReleaseSlot refuses only a spent life or an already-deployed player, so a live un-deployed player can release a BLUFOR slot and claim an OPFOR one; the client is already s_bServed and TBD_MarkerClient.Tick has cancelled itself, so nothing re-requests and the served->unserved clear path in Accept() is unreachable. Recovery is the next map open, but OnMapOpen returns before Request() inside MAP_REQUEST_MIN_GAP_MS (3 s) and stale markers are drawn on open and only replaced a round trip later. THE SERVER SIDE IS SOUND — the verifier could not phrase a cross-side request; this is purely a stale client cache.

T-181.20.notes: Golden fixtures @ bae5d1d1. slot-loadout-coverage.json is the FIRST golden to carry a slot loadout block (all 10 gear refs, cargo at the schema minimum, the primary/optic/magazine triple T-181.10 fixed, plus a no-loadout control); resource names are real vanilla GUIDs from the registry export, not invented. empty-warning-fields.json carries every empty the SCHEMA actually permits. Goldens are globbed (xtask/src/schema_gates.rs:1316) so both are auto-discovered — 4/4 PASS. Twelve negative-control mutants each failed with the exact expected message, proving the loadout fixture reaches the loadout $defs rather than passing vacuously. DISPROVED THE BRIEF'S PREMISE by measurement — see T-181.26 and T-181.31.

T-181.21.notes: ONE-LIFE integrity enforced @ dd79266d. Guard moved to DeployPlayerEx (the actual choke point) returning a new DENIED result, with AdminRespawn as the one documented opt-in bypass. The agent FALSIFIED the brief: death does NOT reach DoSpawn_S (that path is dead on a framework world since audit is swallowed) — it reaches SCR_RespawnComponent.NotifyReadyForSpawn_S, which invites a CLIENT spawn request and would have produced a fully VANILLA body. Closed by overriding CanRequestSpawn_S to refuse any request TBD_SpawnManager did not ticket (epoch-stamped, closed on spawn/kill/disconnect/5s timeout, fails closed). m_mDeadPlayers rekeyed to the durable PlayerBindKey — which required fixing a latent bug first: GetPlayerIdentityId returns a UUID and a NULL uuid formats to the same constant for everyone, so identity-keyed death tracking on the old string test would have made the first death kill the whole server. Also: departed dead players' seats retained (fixes round-never-ends when the last man rage-quits), AdminRespawn is now dead-until-proven-DEPLOYED, AssignSlotForPlayer got real exclusivity + a scanning round-robin. RetryDeploy race closed BY the choke-point guard rather than a duplicate check. UNVERIFIED, highest risk: the 5s possess-ticket window — if the request RPC lands outside it, deploys break outright. Needs a live run.

T-181.22.notes: ONE-LIFE hardened @ 1e301f89. Closed the possess route by modding SCR_PossessSpawnHandlerComponent's CanHandleRequest_S AND HandleRequest_S — calls vanilla routes through unconditionally, so the fix holds whether m_bIgnoreConditions is 0 or 1 (the packed value could not be read offline; it is now self-reported at runtime). Ticket made load-bearing: entity-keyed and consumed once, so a forged RplId matches nothing. Identity policy now matches its comment. adminOverride moved off the public signature so the compiler enforces the single bypass. T-181.41.notes: Worn-kit audit re-homed onto the kit-only path, and the deadline VERIFIED rather than inherited. The resumed agent did not take its predecessor's 'from measurement, not feel' claim on trust — it reproduced the measurement with a temporary probe plus a failing control in the same run, then reverted both and confirmed byte-identical files by md5. The claim HOLDS (kit clothing is synchronous: 17 slots settled on attempt 1 at 250 ms; the control, pointing kit:us_sl at a base character prefab, produced exactly one NAKED ERROR and failed the gate) — but the UPPER BOUND WAS UNDERSTATED. Measured on two independent boots: bodies materialise +2.947/+2.983 s after the line the harness polls for, and 'Game destroyed' lands +2.985/+2.968 s after that. The predecessor wrote that a 3 s deadline 'raced' the kill; it does not race, it LOSES BY 32 ms. The shipped 1 s deadline leaves 1.97 s of margin, and that margin IS TBD_WORLDBOOT_SETTLE — now said out loud in-code. Two structural checks back the design: grep for Callqueue().Remove across the mod (20 hits, none in either touched file) proves the T-181.15 by-function cancel hazard cannot reach the audit ticks; and SpawnEntityPrefab appears exactly once in TBD_SpawnManager, inside SpawnSlotBody, which has two call sites — so coverage is total with no second body path. CORRECTED A PREMISE IN ITS OWN BRIEF: 'world-boot has zero players so the audit never executes there' is FALSE for --mission= mode, because the slot lineup materialises at MISSION START not on join. Recorded one lifetime caveat rather than fixing it on speculation: CallLater holds no reference, so Cancel -> m_bDone -> PruneDoneLoadoutApps can drop the last strong ref with a tick queued. That shape predates this slice, is shared with VerifyTick, and this slice moves exposure DOWN (250 ms vs up to 3 s); reaching it needs a live client, so it is labelled unproven and the note warns that lengthening AUDIT_TICK_MS widens it.

T-181.42.notes: Lobby wire: bijective marker + BOOT-armed self-check + two real bug fixes + the gate flake. SAID PLAINLY THAT THE RENAME ALONE WOULD HAVE BEEN COSMETIC: no committed golden contains a '~', and it independently re-measured split-empties=kept, so the lobby's empty-field handling was already correct and the '~' loss is a latent authoring hazard only. What earns the slice is the other four. FOUND A BUG REACHABLE FROM AUTHORED JSON THE SCHEMA PERMITS: TBD_SpawnManager.BuildSlotRoster formatted slot.Key()/faction/groupCallsign/role into a TSV with NO sanitisation, and mission.schema.json has minLength:1 but NO pattern on any of them — a callsign authored 'AL<TAB>PHA' produced a seven-field row that sailed past the consumer's '<6' guard and shifted every column, so role rendered as 'PHA', the real role was read as the STATE (seat matches neither OPEN nor DEAD, therefore unselectable) and holderId came from 'OPEN'.ToInt() = 0. It hardened the lobby parser to exact arity and reported upstream rather than editing another lane; the command center then fixed it at the source in BuildSlotRoster. Also fixed the same rejected-record cursor bug T-181.26 found in the briefing, gated by a control. FIXED THE world-boot FLAKE, and put the guard in Raise() NOT Start() with a reason: Start() is a one-shot at +2000 ms so gating it on a controller that may not be up yet would mean the picker silently never appears, whereas Tick polls every 500 ms so gating the raise is self-healing. 3/3 FAIL at SETTLE=12 before, 3/3 PASS after. THREE CONTROLS ALL FAILED AS REQUIRED, including one that isolates the cursor fix alone (phase 1 clean, orphanShape lost). OPS CAVEAT WORTH KEEPING: its first control run reported the UNPATCHED verdict — the patch was not live at boot despite a clean compile — so it re-ran verifying the patch present immediately before AND after the boot. A stale-patch run looks exactly like a vacuous check.

T-181.43.notes: wireSafeString pattern ^[^\x00-\x1F\x7F]$ (C0 controls + DEL), shared $def, $ref'd from 10 authored fields. WENT BEYOND THE BRIEF IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION: it constrained group.callsign and role.slot as well, because flatten.rs:518 copies those VERBATIM into slot.groupCallsign/slot.role and interpolates them into slot.id with no re-validation — so constraining only the slot fields would have forbidden the symptom while permitting the cause. Chose the control block over a bare tab/CR/LF blocklist for three reasons it verified rather than asserted: it costs authoring nothing (all four goldens scanned, zero control characters; Alpha-1/2, Saint-Pierre Depot, Cafe, blufor:Alpha:RFL:0 all pass), it is a CLOSED class that cannot drift, and it covers siblings nothing strips today — RosterField and Sanitise each replace exactly \t\n\r, so NUL (a terminator where string.Length() counts BYTES) and VT/FF were undefended. DELIBERATELY DID NOT BAN, each checked in source: '.' (TBD_BriefingData.FIELD_MARK is a bijective per-field PREFIX, so an authored dot cannot confuse a reader), '~' (the RETIRED lossy TBD_LobbyData sentinel — forbidding it would enshrine an abandoned convention), ':' (load-bearing inside slot.id), and the zero-width/bidi class (a display-SPOOFING hazard, not a wire-FRAMING one; folding two defects behind one pattern means a failure stops naming its cause). EXCLUDED briefing.situation/mission/execution with a good reason: they do not ride a delimited wire at all — TBD_BriefingService ships them as parallel array<string> RPC params precisely to preserve paragraph breaks — so a NEWLINE THERE IS LEGITIMATE AUTHORING and constraining it would have broken real missions. TWO must-fail fixtures, not one, because ten $ref sites behind one $def means a single fixture leaves nine free to lose the constraint unnoticed; proven not-false-green by stripping only the pattern line and watching both flip to 'ACCEPTED it — the check this fixture pins is gone'. Two throwaway probes settled silent-loosening risks rather than assuming: minLength:1 as a SIBLING of $ref still applies under 2020-12, and '$' is strict end-of-haystack here (not the PCRE trailing-newline variant). BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THE OPERATOR SHOULD KNOW: /compiled is validated at runtime, so a STORED mission carrying a control character in one of the ten fields now answers 500, and TBD_MissionLoader.OnBackendFetchError discards the body and fails over to its cached copy — the symptom is 'the server is still running the previous mission' with the cause only in the API log. Same shape as T-181.34's enum, and better than a corrupted roster, but real.

T-181.44.notes: Save-time control-char scan + surfacing /compiled rejections. BOTH HALVES, argued: they serve disjoint humans and disjoint failure sets — the mod path is the only place the 500 body reaches the game host and covers rejections the author could never anticipate (a flatten regression, a dangling kit alias, the live faction_eliminated rejection), while the Creator path covers the one class the author can fix, at the moment they can fix it. O(1) CONSTRAINT RESPECTED AND MEASURED: the rule lives in code not the schema, because the schema form costs a per-item object walk plus a regex per slot; instead a single linear pass over the already-parsed serde_json::Value, byte-scanning two short strings per slot (every UTF-8 continuation byte is >= 0x80, so byte scan == char scan over C0+DEL). At 367k slots / 65.7 MB: parse 615.6 ms, scan 34.5 ms = 5.6% of a parse that has to happen anyway. Body capped at 900 B because Print() DISCARDS a line over 1024 B rather than truncating — an uncapped body would log nothing, which is the very failure being fixed. THE LOAD-BEARING TEST is save_scan_agrees_with_the_compiled_schema: it runs the REAL compiler against the REAL schema over a matrix of authored defects and asserts the save-time scan fires exactly when the compiled document would be rejected, both directions, with anti-vacuity guards (>=4 cases must reach the schema pattern, >=2 must compile clean) so an A==B over cases that never fire cannot pass. Integration test proven failing on base: 201 CREATED with a tab stored in the callsign.

T-181.45.notes: 10 .meta sidecars for the input .conf files. CONFResourceClass is not a guess — enumerated every *ResourceClass string in the server binary; there is no Action/ActionContext-specific class. RETIRED A RECORDED LANDMINE: '.meta is only honoured after Workbench rewrites the rdb' is FALSE. Proved with two probes on a loose addon — repointed a .meta to a GUID present nowhere in the rdb and the world still loaded by that GUID, then pointed scenarioId at one of the NEW GUIDs and the engine echoed the path back and reached class inspection, which it could only do from a GUID->path mapping the new sidecar supplied. So the engine scans and reads .meta at startup; no operator pass needed. ALSO ESTABLISHED registration alone IS enough here, unlike the menu presets: vanilla's gproj names only three Configs/System resources (two single-valued InputManagerSettings fields a mod cannot append to, plus the MenuConfigs list), and its own 26 ActionContext confs and all Actions confs appear nowhere in it — the directory is the contract. Data/*.json correctly left alone, TESTED not assumed: added a JSONResourceClass sidecar for registry.json and reproduced the identical failure, because TBD_Registry.Load uses FileIO.FileExists on a $TBD_Framework: alias — a filesystem call, not a resource lookup, so GUID identity is irrelevant to it.

T-181.46.notes: NOT AUTHORING — A COMPILER BUG. The operator asked to drop faction_eliminated from their mission and it turned out not to be theirs to drop: winConditions is SYNTHESIZED in flatten.rs, which documents at :430 that the editor never authors it, and end_on was the hardcoded literal ['time_limit','faction_eliminated'] for EVERY mission. So every single-faction mission was unloadable — TBD_MissionValidator rejects the document, the server parks in LOADING, and the author has no field to edit. Fixed by declaring faction_eliminated only when at least two factions actually HOLD SLOTS, counted over the flattened slots rather than factions[] because a faction can be declared with zero seats, which is exactly the shape that surfaced it. Regression test proven to FAIL without the change ('one-sided mission must not declare faction_eliminated: [time_limit, faction_eliminated]') and pass with it; 38/38 lib tests green. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL EARNED ITS KEEP TWICE: (1) `cargo build -p map-engine-core` compiles NOTHING in src/mission/** because the module is behind #[cfg(feature = "mission")] which is off by default — a deliberate syntax error built clean in 0.07s and exit 0, so the first version of this fix was entirely unverified and would have shipped that way. The real build is `--features mission`, or just build website-api. (2) With the feature on, the build immediately caught a borrow error the eye had missed: `slots: doc_slots` moves the vec before win_conditions could read it, so the count had to move above the struct literal. RELATED, STILL OPEN: `flow` is hardcoded in the same place (briefingSeconds 600, safeStartSeconds 300, timeLimitSeconds 5400, jip until_safestart_end) — which is why every golden carries those exact numbers, and why T-181.38 parses values no author can currently set.

T-181.47.notes: Rebuilt the UI layout foundation on the idiom shipped layouts actually use. ROOT CAUSE WAS ONE EMPTY BLOCK: TBD_ListRow.layout had `Slot ButtonWidgetSlot { }` with no HorizontalAlign, and a child with no align keeps its DESIRED size — which for the FrameWidgetClass inside it is ZERO. So every row collapsed to a sliver, and with no `Wrap 0` the text wrapped one character per line: the vertical column the operator saw. Same defect class 6x in the shell, where four button Body/Background/Label widgets had NO Slot block at all. HorizontalAlign 3 = Stretch CONFIRMED from vanilla_reference/Scripts/Core/generated/UI/LayoutHorizontalAlign.c rather than inferred from CRF frequency. Row body is now SizeLayout > Overlay > (Background, Accent, HorizontalLayout) because Overlay is the stacking primitive and stretches while a Frame has no intrinsic size; Title/Detail ride LayoutSlot { SizeMode Fill FillWeight 1 }. CORRECTED THE COMMAND CENTER'S ORACLE: the brief said Anchor/SizeX/SizeY are absent from the engine string table and therefore invalid — but with controls, ImageWidgetClass, TextWidgetClass, HorizontalAlign, Padding and HeightOverride ALL miss too and are all valid, so a miss is evidence of nothing; and the first probe returned a SILENT all-miss because `strings` is absent in the container with stderr suppressed. Anchor IS honoured, proven by PrimaryAction (Anchor 1 1 1 1, OffsetLeft -288) rendering bottom-right on the operator's screen. Built scripts/mod/verify-ui-layouts.sh (brace balance, slot-class whitelist, geometry invariant, container children missing a slot or an align, and the FindAnyWidget name contract) — and its FIRST CUT PASSED THE KNOWN-BROKEN FILES because GUID strings desynced the brace counter; fixed, it lands C6 on TBD_ListRow.layout:13, the exact empty slot block, and rejects five injected defects one per arm. Now gate step 6 of 12. Widget-name contract preserved with zero renames, 16 names. ADMITTED GUESSES, each with blast radius: `Size 3 44` for the accent rail, AlignableSlot for SizeLayout/ScrollLayout children (their specific slot classes exist in the generated API but appear in NO shipped layout), the 2px row-gap padding, and FocusAnchor deliberately not added.

T-181.48.notes: The picker and the auto-deploy wave cannot both be on. m_bAutoDeploy shipped as 1 and TBD_GameMode.et never overrode it, so the dev wave seated everyone ~250ms into LOBBY; T-181.29's ShouldStandDown() then closed the picker ~500ms after it opened. T-181.49.notes: Make the lobby raise path survivable and observable. MEASURED: TBD_GameMode is constructed TWICE per Workbench session (World Editor 20:39:34, Play 20:39:59) while all TBD_LobbyStage state is static and survives between them. TBD_LobbyStage.Start is a one-shot CallLater(...,false) behind three guards that log NOTHING, and it fires ~200ms BEFORE the framework manager is ready (Start ~20:40:01.32 vs roll-call 20:40:01.523) - losing that race is permanent and silent. T-181.50.notes: Pre-slot body + kill the vanilla loading placeholder. Vanilla SCR_RespawnSystemComponent.OnInit:270 builds a loading splash DIRECTLY on the workspace (above menu-manager menus) and mutes SFX; it is destroyed ONLY from the vanilla spawn pipeline, which we bypass and actively block in CanRequestSpawn_S. Our modded class overrides OnPlayerRegistered_S/OnPlayerAuditSuccess_S/CanRequestSpawn_S but NOT OnInit, so nothing ever tears it down. T-181.51.notes: Two backend calls share ONE root cause, not two URL typos. ServiceAuth (middleware/auth.rs:108) reads only x-service-token; TBD_MissionListLoader:99 and TBD_RosterLoader:127 both send 'Authorization, Bearer' while the three loaders that work all send X-Service-Token. T-181.52.notes: Log-noise demotion + oracle lane gap. Demote the magazine first-attempt 'mount refused' line from WARNING to INFO (the deterministic-swap design intends it; it reads as a fault). So the ghost's value was defensive and unproven while its cost was a modal dialog mid-mission, which would be fatal in a live event. T-181.54.notes: Correct a mission-loader warning that told the operator a falsehood, and add scripts/mod/test-mission.sh. OPERATOR-REPORTED LIVE: staging a golden produced 'RUNNING A CACHED MISSION - this is the last document the backend served successfully, NOT THE ONE CONFIGURED'. That last clause can NEVER be true: LoadFromProfileFile reads $profile:missions/<missionId>.json, so the file is KEYED BY the configured id and the mission identity always matches. What can differ is the VERSION. Worse, it labelled a deliberate stage as a fault. MEASURED discriminator against the live API: a golden's msn_* id returns 400 {invalid id} because the API validates the id SHAPE before lookup, while a valid-but-absent uuid returns 404 {mission not found} - so 400 means this id was never a backend mission and the disk file is intended, not stale. Loader now threads the http code into TryProfileFallbackAfterRestFailure and branches: 400 -> event-level 'staged on disk' note (plus the no-schema-validation caveat), anything else -> the stale-VERSION warning. (2) `foreach (string cls, array<BaseContainer> bucket : comps)` iterates a map keyed by component CLASS. tickets.title: server_fps type mismatch silently blanks the whole Server Intel page
tickets.summary:
REPRODUCED by T-194 against a populated fixture, not inferred. models/telemetry.rs:102 serializes numeric(5,1) cast to float8; frontend/src/dto.rs:101 deserializes i64. A probe using the DTO verbatim: 'TBD Primary — Everon server_fps: 58.7 -> DROPPED (invalid type: floating point `58.7`, expected i64)'. Both read sites swallow the error — server_intel.rs:150 uses .ok() and sse.rs:80 uses `if let Ok(...)` — so against a COMPLETE, HEALTHY frame the page renders 0/0 players and '—' for uptime, FPS, time and weather, and the SSE stream reports connected while updating nothing. The whole page looks like a dead server. Fix the DTO to f64 (do not round the wire value). NOTE: the R-api golden gate CANNOT catch this — it types /servers as DataEnvelope<Value>, so the round-trip passes while the real DTO fails. Consider typing that fixture properly at the same time.

INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED STILL LIVE by T-232 (2026-07-26), which found it from the frontend side and added a dimension the original filing missed:

`sse.rs:80` does `if let Ok(json) = serde_json::from_str::<ServerStatusDto>(...)`, so EVERY LIVE TELEMETRY SSE FRAME SILENTLY FAILS TO DESERIALIZE AND IS DROPPED. Not just the Server Intel page render — the whole realtime stream is inert while reporting connected. T-232 also traced the same root cause to a confident `FPS: 0` on the dashboard card for a healthy server, which it fixed locally; the DTO itself (dto.rs:101 `pub server_fps: i64` against models/telemetry.rs:131 f64 over numeric(5,1)) was outside its ownership and is still wrong.

Two independent agents have now reached this from opposite directions. Fix the DTO to f64 and do NOT round the wire value.

SHIPPED 2026-07-26. Wire bytes captured off a live stack: `"server_fps":58.7`. Before, that exact frame through the real DTO gave `invalid type: floating point 58.7, expected i64 at line 1 column 121`. After, both the frame and the committed GET__servers.json pass.

BROWSER-VERIFIED before/after on the same build, same stack, same frame — the page really did render a healthy server as dead: players 0 -> 47, max /0 -> /64, uptime — -> 05:30:42, FPS — -> 58.7 (Optimal), simulated time — -> 06:42, conditions — -> overcast, status dot offline-yellow -> success. The row itself loaded in both cases (IP and modpack name present in the DOM), so this was the DTO and not a fetch failure.

ZERO other ServerStatusDto fields mismatched — all ten swept against models/telemetry.rs AND the server_statuses columns. It also REMOVED the `#[serde(flatten)] extra` catch-all: nothing in the SPA ever read it, and leaving it would have let the newly-typed golden pass the day the backend grew a field. That does not loosen the live read (serde ignores unknown fields anyway) — it makes the GATE strict.

THE SWALLOWED ERRORS, decided per site rather than blanket-logged:
  sse.rs:80 — decode_frame is now pure, returning Rejected{error,payload} instead of None; the loop warns and sets the error signal. `connected` STAYS true because it IS connected — claiming otherwise would be a second lie. The last good status is kept, not cleared. The warn is DEDUPED (first occurrence of each distinct error, then powers of ten) because a schema mismatch fails EVERY frame and a per-frame warn buries its own message in seconds.
  server_intel.rs:150 — deliberately NOT blanket-logged. `.ok()` was conflating `"status": null` (a server with no telemetry row — the golden's third row is exactly this, so warning would cry wolf on every render) with a PRESENT but unparseable object (a real contract breach). Split: absent silent, present-but-unparseable audited.

A STRUCTURAL INSIGHT WORTH KEEPING: the decode lives in dto.rs, not sse.rs, because `mod sse` is #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")] in main.rs — so ANY test module inside it is never compiled by `cargo test`. A frame-decode policy nobody can test is how this defect stayed invisible for a month. Seven new tests now run natively.

THE GOLDEN GATE — the more valuable half, and enumerated rather than eyeballed. Every `api_get::<T>` cross-referenced against its r_api test: SIX goldens were `Value` while a DTO read them live. All six typed. Typing them found TWO MORE latent drifts nobody had hit — EventListItem::percent was f64 over an integer wire (the golden's `37` re-serialised as `37.0`), and OrbatSlot::assigned_to carried skip_serializing_if over a field the backend emits as explicit null.

It also distinguished escape hatches from accurate statements: /announcements, /wiki, /vehicle-database, /modpacks and /admin/audit-logs stay `Value` because they have NO typed consumer, and three of them are not fetched by any page at all. Each test now says so. And the SSE payload had NO FIXTURE OF ANY KIND — the corpus is all GET bodies — so one captured live frame is now pinned as LIVE_SSE_FRAME.

tickets.title: PUT /missions/:id/armory with an empty body DELETEs the whole armory
tickets.summary: FOUND by T-218's #[serde(default)] sweep, same shape as T-185 and T-218 on a different table. handlers/missions.rs:683 — SetArmoryInput.items carries #[serde(default)], and the handler runs an UNCONDITIONAL `DELETE FROM mission_armories WHERE mission_id = $1` before inserting. Highest severity of the 10 instances the sweep turned up. Fix: make `items` required (drop the default) so `{}` is a decode error, and reject with 400 rather than defaulting. Verify by seeding rows, POSTing `{}`, and asserting the rows survive.

tickets.title: Telemetry re-ingest reverts a completed match and zeroes player stats
tickets.summary:
FOUND by T-218's sweep. Three defaulted structs in handlers/telemetry.rs reach destructive writes and do NOT self-heal:
  :172-177 MatchInput.outcome / winning_faction / aar_replay_url — re-POSTing a match id with a partial body reverts a completed, won match to `pending` with no winner and drops the AAR link.
  :186-196 PlayerStatInput counters — re-ingest zeroes kills/deaths/etc, and that propagates into `users` stats and the leaderboard materialized view.
  :41-57 ServerStatusInput — a partial heartbeat writes a permanent `player_count=0, server_fps=0` history sample and fires a false `server.low_fps` audit WARN.
These are service-token endpoints, so a game-server bug or a retried request corrupts history silently. Fix: require the fields, or make the writes COALESCE-style partial updates. Decide per field which is right — a heartbeat legitimately omits fields; a match result does not.

tickets.title: Ban reason erased on re-ban; malformed body still bans
tickets.summary: FOUND by T-218's sweep. handlers/admin.rs:168 collapses the JsonRejection instead of returning 400, so a malformed or wrong-Content-Type body still executes `UPDATE users SET is_banned=true, ban_reason=$1` with an empty reason — erasing a prior reason on re-ban and leaving an unexplained ban in the audit trail. Two-part fix: `map_err` the extractor like the other ~25 handlers in the crate, AND drop the #[serde(default)] on BanInput.reason at :155 — a well-formed `{}` does the same damage. Same pattern T-218 closed in approvals.rs; this is the last extractor-collapse site.

tickets.title: Event registration upsert orphans an ORBAT seat nobody can free
tickets.summary: FOUND by T-218's sweep. handlers/events.rs:786 collapses the JsonRejection for RegisterBody, so a bad body still runs the registration upsert and sets an existing row's `slot_id = NULL` while `orbat_slots.assigned_to` still names the user. `withdraw` only releases the seat via `if let Some(sid)`, so with slot_id NULL it takes no action: the seat reads as occupied forever and the occupant cannot release it. Requires an admin DB edit to unstick. Fix the extractor (map_err → 400), and separately make withdraw fall back to clearing orbat_slots.assigned_to by user id so already-orphaned seats can be freed.

tickets.title: Unguarded defaulted fields reshuffle the wiki nav and blank a character name

tickets.title: Editor gate harness wedges on /missions/:id/edit — every browser leg is unverifiable
tickets.summary:
PROVEN PRE-EXISTING by T-221 via A/B, not inferred. `gate smoke persist`, `gate doctor` and `render-check` against /missions/smoke/edit all fail with Page.loadEventFired / Runtime.evaluate timeouts. T-221 checked out HEAD~1's yrs_persist.rs, rebuilt, and the baseline dist wedges IDENTICALLY — so this is not that slice's doing. Also unchanged by serving map assets, by debug vs release dist, and by chromium-1223 vs 1228. The non-editor route / loads and evaluates fine, so CDP itself works; it is specific to the editor page. `gate doctor` reports FAIL on liveness with zero strays and 20 GB free, so its own diagnosis is not the answer either.

WHY THIS IS PRIORITY 0: it is not one ticket's problem. Every remaining frontend ticket that needs a browser assertion — persistence round-trips, editor smokes, render checks — can only be verified by reasoning while this is wedged. T-221 had a complete probe written (plant a legacy record, assert it is withheld-and-warned, adopt, assert the scoped key appears, assert a second account sees none of it) and could not run a line of it. That probe needs no new files — `gate render-check --assert-js` takes it — so fixing the harness immediately buys back a real verification that is currently owed.

Start from docs/website/EDITOR_GATE_RUNBOOK.md and the gate doctor liveness check (apps/website/frontend doctor.rs:166-172). Bisect what the editor route does at load that / does not: wasm size, the wgpu context, or a hung fetch.

SOLVED 2026-07-26. ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT A WEDGE — the browser process was DYING. Chromium takes SIGABRT ~300ms after navigating /missions/smoke/edit, at third_party/skia/src/ports/SkFontMgr_FontConfigInterface.cpp:163 "Not implemented" — the unconditional SK_ABORT in onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter (per-character font fallback). Captured from chromium's own stderr with the `Received signal 6` stack, plus a gdb attach showing the abort on a ThreadPoolForeg thread of the BROWSER process. A dead browser never answers the websocket, and cdp.rs's reader leaves the pending call in the map, so it surfaced as a Runtime.evaluate timeout.

PRECONDITION: chromium resolved NO FONT AT ALL. `~/.cache/fontconfig` is shared between the Fedora host and the Debian 12 distrobox (same $HOME) and contains only the container's directory-hash entries. Chromium's bundled fontconfig accepts them, writes nothing, and never rescans — so it starts with zero fonts while `fc-list` on the host reports 783.

ISOLATION, all arms identical but the variable: shared cache + editor -> FATAL; a COPY of that cache at a new path + editor -> FATAL; an EMPTY cache dir + editor -> no fatal, 10/10 evals; shared cache + `/` -> no fatal. So it is cache CONTENT, not path, not URL length, not the API. Falsified along the way: URL length, --headless=old, --enable-unsafe-webgpu, extensions, and every single-character page tried. Route matrix: /, /dashboard, /missions, /missions/smoke, /vehicles, /mortar all survive the broken font environment — ONLY the mission editor reaches a per-character fallback. That is exactly why it read as editor-specific and app-side, and why it was invariant to map assets, debug-vs-release dist, and chromium 1223 vs 1228.

T-177's earlier 'fix the shell crash by using the full chrome' only MOVED this: onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter is unimplemented in both builds.

FIX: the gate owns its own fontconfig cache ($TMPDIR/tbd-gate-cache) via doctor.rs ensure_gate_font_cache(), called from Harness::new so every smoke, render-check and r-auth inherits it. Plus three new doctor checks — `fonts`, `dist` (a missing --dist used to 500 everything and then fail on LIVENESS, reading as 'the editor wedged'), and liveness now asks /json/version so it prints 'the headless browser process DIED' instead of 'timed out'.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY from the command center: `gate doctor: OK`, with `liveness  editor page booted; evaluate responsive`. It was FAIL.

AND IT PAID THE DEBT: T-221's persistence probe ran for real — `gate render-check --seed-auth --assert-js`, 30 assertions, PASS=true. Legacy record withheld-and-warned, adopt claimed 1, scoped keys present, restore/undoRestore round-tripped, second account saw none of it. Dist provenance checked: wasm md5 identical to the operator's live dist, so no stale cross-worktree artifact.

OPERATOR NOTE: `rm -rf ~/.cache/fontconfig` fixes this outside the gate, but any fontconfig run inside the Debian container re-poisons it. The gate no longer depends on it either way.

tickets.title: Every map placement mints a fresh ORBAT squad, so the tree grows a squad per click
tickets.summary:
FOUND by T-308 while fixing Apply Template; reported, not touched (out of its owns). place_orbat.rs:52-55 mints a NEW squad on every single placement. That is why '>1 squad under a side' — which T-217's guard treats as authored structure worth refusing over — is actually the normal state after two clicks. T-308 worked around it by folding machine-minted squads (one slot, still on the default `Squad {n}` label, no callsign, no vehicles) into the apply target, which is correct as far as it goes but is a workaround.

If a placement instead appended to the side's current squad, or to an explicit active squad, the fold in orbat_apply_faction would be near-dead code and the ORBAT tree would stop growing a squad per click. Decide the model — implicit 'current squad' vs an explicit active-squad selection in the ORBAT panel — then make placement honour it. Keep T-308's fold as the compatibility path for documents already carrying per-click squads.

tickets.title: `make api` builds into the shared target dir and can serve unmerged slice code
tickets.summary:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-07-26 by the slice agent, which DISPROVED the diagnosis this ticket was filed on. Recorded in full because the wrong version was stated confidently to the operator and must not become received wisdom.

WHAT I CLAIMED: the operator's dev API on :8080 died at 08:28:10 because a slice rebuilt website-api into the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR, overwriting the running binary's ELF in place. The binary's mtime matched the death exactly.

WHY THAT IS WRONG, measured two ways by the agent and then re-confirmed independently:
  1. Rebuilding into the directory a process runs from does NOT kill it. Cargo unlinks and re-hardlinks; the live process keeps its old inode. Demonstrated: API on :18322, `cargo build --bin api` into the same dir, inode 52999571 -> 53011660, /proc/PID/exe became `(deleted)`, /healthz stayed 200 throughout.
  2. The kernel forbids the in-place write anyway — `cp` and `dd conv=notrunc` over a running, still-linked ELF both fail ETXTBSY (Text file busy).
  3. Re-confirmed from the command center at 09:06: PID 52467 started 08:52:33 from target/debug/api, that path was rewritten by the gate at 08:54:46, and it is STILL SERVING from `(deleted)`. The mtime match was correlation.

THE REAL CAUSE OF THE 08:28:10 DEATH IS UNDETERMINED. No OOM, segfault, or API entry in journalctl 08:25-08:32; tbd_reforger_db has been up 42h healthy, so not a DB restart. The remaining candidate the agent could not rule out: `make api` runs a FOREGROUND `cargo run`, which dies on SIGHUP when its terminal or session ends. Note the hand-placed band-aid used `setsid nohup ... & disown`, which is exactly the SIGHUP remedy — so the band-aid may have been fixing the right problem for the wrong stated reason. IF THE BAND-AID IS RETIRED, KEEP RUNNING `make api` DETACHED.

WHAT THIS TICKET ACTUALLY FIXES, and it is real and measured: which commands emit target/debug/api — `cargo check` does NOT; `cargo test -p website-api` DOES; `cargo build --bin api` DOES. The wave gate runs `cargo test -p website-api` after every land, all night, so the shared target/debug/api belongs to whichever tree built last and a dev server on it serves UNMERGED SLICE CODE. That is T-300, and isolating `make api` closes it. It also drops `make api` out of the shared build-lock queue behind seven agents.

Cost measured: cold build 25s / 322 crates, warm rebuild 0.98s, 2.1 GB disk. .gitignore needed no entry — `target-*/` at :46 already covers it. wave.sh deliberately NOT changed: the gate does write that path but cannot kill anything, and isolating the single consumer beats policing an unbounded set of producers.

tickets.title: Admin ban button sends `{}` and now 400s — the ban UI is broken on main
tickets.summary:
CAUSED BY T-317, which landed at 62a804e4 and correctly made `reason` required on POST /admin/users/:id/ban. The frontend was not updated in the same wave because it is a different file with a different owner.

apps/website/frontend/src/personnel.rs:342-378 prompts "Ban reason (optional):" and DELIBERATELY sends `serde_json::json!({})` when the operator leaves it empty. That path now returns 400 and the UI shows a flat "Ban failed" with no explanation. A normal ban WITH a reason still works — `api_post_ok` uses gloo-net `.json()`, which sets the Content-Type header — so this is the empty-reason path only.

The backend is right and should not be reverted: an unexplained ban is exactly what T-317 set out to stop. The UI is what is stale. Make the reason required client-side too: change the prompt copy off "(optional)", reject or re-prompt on empty rather than posting `{}`, and surface the server's actual error message instead of a flat "Ban failed" — the 400 body already carries a usable one.

Found and reported by the T-317 agent, which correctly refused to edit a file it did not own.

tickets.title: Claiming a second ORBAT seat does not release the first, so one user holds two
tickets.summary:
FOUND by T-318 while fixing the orphan bug, and it is the bigger half. MEASURED, not inferred: claim slot0, then claim slot1, both with entirely VALID requests — the user ends up holding 2 seats while their registration row names 1. Pre-fix, withdraw then left one stranded.

So T-318's part 1 (rejecting malformed bodies) does not stop all new orphans, only the accidental ones. The valid-request path mints them too. T-318's withdraw fix makes them recoverable — it releases by occupant, and its test asserts BOTH seats are freed — but the seat is wrongly occupied until someone withdraws, and a capacity display reading it will be wrong meanwhile.

Fixing it properly means reconciling `assigned_to` inside register's existing `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` transaction and deciding the waitlist interaction. That is a design change to a concurrency-sensitive handler, not a line edit — which is why T-318 reported it rather than folding it in.

Two related structural notes from the same agent, both worth resolving with this:
  - `withdraw` does NOT take the `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on `event_missions` that `register` does, though both do check-then-write on capacity.
  - `event_registrations.slot_id` and `orbat_slots.assigned_to` are a denormalized duplicate of ONE fact with no constraint forcing agreement. A partial unique index on `orbat_slots(event_mission_id, assigned_to) WHERE assigned_to IS NOT NULL` would make double-claiming impossible at the DB level. That is a migration, so it wants coordinating with T-228, which owns apps/website/api/migrations.

tickets.title: Two telemetry models are non-Option String over nullable columns
tickets.summary:
PREMISE FALSE — the agent refused the stated fix and was right. Kept in full because the wrong version was mine.

I claimed a NULL in matches.winning_faction or match_player_stats.role_played would 500 the read path, held safe only by T-316 politely writing ''. Measured: `GET /api/v1/me/deployments` returns **200**. The only read of either struct — deployments.rs:127 and :134 — already COALESCEs both columns (plus aar_replay_url and created_at). The safety was never on the write side; it is in the query. Stronger: the operator's live DB ALREADY HOLDS a real NULL in matches.winning_faction (rf-match-20260726-01, outcome pending) plus two NULL aar_replay_urls, and has been serving 200 the whole time.

The mismatch is nonetheless real — dropping the COALESCE in a probe against those same rows gives `unexpected null; try decoding as an Option` for both columns. But Option<String> is the WRONG fix, and this is the durable part: the wire cannot express the distinction it would add. `skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty"` already omits the key for "", byte-identically to an omitted None, so None and "" would be two encodings of one state. The committed golden GET__me__deployments.json proves it — its first record came from a row whose aar_replay_url IS NULL and the golden simply lacks the key. "No winner" is also already carried by `outcome`, and T-316 designated "" as the clear-the-winner re-adjudication signal.

Correct fix is at the schema (NOT NULL DEFAULT '' after a backfill), which is T-228's directory — handed to it. What shipped here is comment-only: the invariant, the measured evidence and the rejected alternative, recorded in models/telemetry.rs where the next person writes a read query. No type, no serde attribute, no wire byte changed.

THE REAL PAYLOAD was the sweep: three genuine 500s elsewhere in the same class, all captured live — T-329 (dashboard, FIRING IN PRODUCTION for two real users), T-307 (events briefing, reachable from any fresh seed), T-330 (approvals updated_at, latent). And tests/null_tolerance.rs, which exists for exactly this class, misses all three.

tickets.title: Matches played before an identity link never backfill, so deployments undercount
tickets.summary:
SPLIT FROM T-231 (c). VERIFIED by the T-231 agent: there is NO `UPDATE match_player_stats` anywhere in apps/website/api/ — zero hits across the crate.

telemetry.rs:376-381 resolves `discord_id` at INGEST time. So every match a player played before linking their identity keeps `discord_id = NULL` forever. `recompute_user_stats` (telemetry.rs:530-534) counts only non-NULL rows, so those matches never reach `total_deployments` — a player who links after three ops shows zero deployments and their service record is permanently short.

This is not a corruption bug, it is a missing step: nothing ever goes back and claims the historical rows once the link exists. Fix is one statement in the existing confirm transaction in `handlers/me.rs` — UPDATE match_player_stats SET discord_id = ... WHERE arma_id = ... AND discord_id IS NULL — followed by a recompute. Do it inside the transaction that consumes the link code, so a failure cannot half-link.

Check whether attendance/leaderboard rows need the same treatment, and whether unlinking (if that exists) should reverse it.

tickets.title: `#tbd link` code is visible in chat before TBD can suppress it
tickets.summary:
SPLIT FROM T-231 (b). The agent verified the load-bearing claim AT THE CALL SITE rather than trusting the header: TBD_AdminCommands.c:30-46 calls `super.OnNewMessage(...)` at line 32, BEFORE `TBD_IdentityLink.TryHandleChat(...)` at line 45. The message is already distributed by the time TBD sees it, so returning true suppresses NOTHING. There is no script-side fix.

Existing mitigations are correct and complete for a chat surface and should NOT be redone: the usage text warns, every failure path emits NewCodeAdvice(), success consumes the code in the same transaction so a leaked code is single-use and already spent, and the code is never logged (the HTTP_CODE_NULL branch deliberately drops the body because GetData() returns the REQUEST on transport failure).

The real fix is an in-game UI field instead of a chat line, which is blocked on `resourceDatabase.rdb` regeneration — the same blocker TBD_AdminScreen carries (TBD_AdminCommands.c:23-25). OPERATOR/WORKBENCH ONLY.

tickets.title: mcpd runs long-lived from the shared target dir, so it can serve unmerged code
tickets.summary:
FOUND by T-322 while isolating `make api`; flagged not fixed, different owner.

`mcpd` (scripts/mod/mcp-daemon.sh) is the second long-lived process running out of the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR, with a 4h max-life. It carries the same correctness exposure `make api` just had: the wave gate's `cargo test -p website-api` rewrites binaries in that tree after every land, so a daemon started before a land keeps running one tree's code while the repo has moved on.

Note what T-322 established, so this is not fixed for the wrong reason: a rebuild does NOT kill a running process (cargo unlinks and re-links; the process keeps its inode, and the kernel refuses an in-place overwrite with ETXTBSY). The risk is STALENESS, not death — the daemon silently serving code that is no longer what main says.

Apply the same fix: an inline CARGO_TARGET_DIR on whatever builds it, matching the shape used for `api`/`rust-api` in the Makefile and for target-gate-frontend / dist-gate-frontend in wave.sh.

tickets.title: GET /api/v1/dashboard 500s in production for two real users
tickets.summary:
FIRING RIGHT NOW ON LIVE DATA. Found by T-325's sweep and captured, not inferred:
  `error occurred while decoding column "callsign": unexpected null`

handlers/dashboard.rs:101 does `SELECT orbat_slots.*`. It is the ONLY one of six OrbatSlot read sites that uses a bare `*` instead of the coalescing column list — the other five, e.g. deployments.rs:103, spell the columns out and COALESCE the nullable ones.

In the operator's `tbd_reforger` today: 9 of 16 orbat_slots rows carry a NULL in callsign/loadout/tag, and TWO of those have `assigned_to` set. So GET /api/v1/dashboard 500s right now for discord_ids ...002 and ...005. The dashboard is the landing page after login.

Fix is small: copy the coalescing column list from deployments.rs:103. Do NOT 'fix' it by making the model fields Option — T-325 established why that is wrong (the wire cannot express the distinction; `skip_serializing_if = String::is_empty` already omits the key, so None and "" would be two encodings of one state, and the committed goldens depend on the current shape).

ALSO IN SCOPE, because it is the reason this survived: tests/null_tolerance.rs is a purpose-built regression suite for exactly this bug class and MISSES all three instances T-325 found. It also never touches `matches` or `match_player_stats` at all. Extend it so this class cannot recur silently — that is worth more than the one-line query fix.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS TICKET, from the agent that fixed it. The captured error I quoted names the WRONG COLUMN: `callsign` is NOT NULL on all 18 of the operator's orbat_slots rows. It is `tag` that is NULL — on 9 rows, including exactly the two with assigned_to set. Users and mechanism right, column wrong. And there are SEVEN OrbatSlot read sites, not six; dashboard.rs was the only bare one, the other six all coalesce.

WHY null_tolerance.rs MISSED ALL THREE — three structural failures, not a forgotten case:
  1. It LISTED endpoints — 5 of 44 GET routes, and none of the three defects lived in those 5.
  2. ITS ROWS WERE UNREACHABLE. It authenticated as dev-login (...001) but seeded rows against ...099, and never set orbat_slots.assigned_to. Every `WHERE assigned_to = $me` branch — exactly where this bug lived — was dead. Calling /dashboard would have passed VACUOUSLY. tests/dashboard_reads.rs:80 still does that today.
  3. It LISTED tables, never inserting matches/match_player_stats at all, and ASSUMED omitting an INSERT column yields NULL — true only while no nullable column has a DEFAULT, and never verified.

Now it mints its own session so caller-scoped predicates resolve to its own rows; NULLs every nullable column from information_schema by explicit UPDATE and asserts the NULLs landed; sweeps every GET route with a guard that parses src/app.rs and fails when a route is added uncovered; and adds a STATIC ENUMERATOR cross-referencing every SELECT literal in src/ against information_schema, failing on a bare `*` or an un-COALESCEd nullable column. That half needs no predicate, so it reaches handlers no test exercises. Proven: reinstating the bare `*` turns both red, the static one naming the file and line. Catches all three known instances, each by both halves independently.

Honest about residual gaps: select lists assembled past their literal prefix (QueryBuilder::push), untyped query/query_scalar, and non-GET handlers behaviourally (three OrbatSlot reads live in POST handlers, caught only by the static half).

tickets.title: GET /api/v1/approvals 500s on a NULL mission updated_at
tickets.summary:
FOUND by T-325's sweep, captured not inferred: `error occurred while decoding column "updated_at": unexpected null` from handlers/approvals.rs:55, which selects a bare `m.updated_at` where the sibling read sites COALESCE.

Latent on the operator's data today — `missions` has no NULL updated_at there — but it is the same defect as T-329 (live) and T-307 (reachable from any fresh seed), and 'latent' here means 'nothing has written that value yet', not 'cannot happen'.
